l_on.title: Make sure Wi-Fi is on and Airplane mode is off
l_on.text: Check the Wi-Fi switch in the system menu. Some laptops also have a Wi-Fi key (an antenna symbol on a function key) or a small switch on the side that turns the radio off completely.

paths.win11: Quick settings (network icon on the taskbar) > Wi-Fi and Airplane mode tiles
paths.win10: Network icon on the taskbar > Wi-Fi and Airplane mode buttons
paths.macnew: Control Center > Wi-Fi (or System Settings > Wi-Fi)
paths.macold: Wi-Fi icon in the menu bar > Turn Wi-Fi On

l_adapter.title: Check the Wi-Fi adapter
l_adapter.text: On Windows, open Device Manager and expand Network adapters. Look for an entry with Wireless, Wi-Fi or 802.11 in its name. A small down-arrow means it is disabled (right-click > Enable device); a yellow warning sign means a driver problem; no such entry at all means Windows does not see the hardware. On a Mac, hold Option and click the Wi-Fi icon in the menu bar to see the interface details; if macOS reports no Wi-Fi hardware, contact Apple Support.

paths.win11: Right-click Start > Device Manager > Network adapters
paths.win10: Right-click Start > Device Manager > Network adapters
paths.macnew: Option-click the Wi-Fi icon in the menu bar
paths.macold: Option-click the Wi-Fi icon in the menu bar

l_adapter.undo: If you enabled the adapter, you can disable it again with the same right-click menu.

l_driver.title: Update the Wi-Fi driver from the right source
l_driver.text: Install drivers only from Windows Update (optional updates) or from the laptop maker's official support website for your exact model. Avoid driver updater tools and download portals. On a Mac, Wi-Fi drivers come with macOS updates.

paths.win11: Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Optional updates
paths.win10: Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update > View optional updates

l_driver.undo: Windows: Device Manager > Network adapters > Wi-Fi adapter > Properties > Driver > Roll Back Driver (when available).

l_close.title: Test right next to the router
l_close.text: Carry the laptop into the same room as the router and refresh the network list. Walls, floors, mirrors, aquariums and metal furniture weaken Wi-Fi a lot, and 5 GHz and 6 GHz signals fade faster than 2.4 GHz.

l_band.title: Check bands and hidden networks
l_band.text: Routers send on 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz; newer ones also on 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E and 7). An older laptop that lacks a band can't see a network that only uses it. A hidden network (name not broadcast) never appears in the list – it has to be added by name.

paths.win11: Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > Add network
paths.win10: Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > Add a new network
paths.macnew: System Settings > Wi-Fi > Other… (join a hidden network)
paths.macold: Wi-Fi icon in the menu bar > Join Other Network…

l_forget.title: Forget the network on the laptop
l_forget.text: A saved profile with an old password or old security settings makes the laptop fail silently or ask for the password again and again. Removing it lets you join fresh.

paths.win11: Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > (your network) > Forget
paths.win10: Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi > Manage known networks > (your network) > Forget
paths.macnew: System Settings > Wi-Fi > Details… (or the … button) next to your network > Forget This Network
paths.macold: System Preferences > Network > Wi-Fi > Advanced > select the network > minus (–) > OK > Apply

l_forget.undo: Choose the network in the Wi-Fi list again and enter its password.

l_password.title: Enter the password carefully
l_password.text: Wi-Fi passwords are case-sensitive; 0 and O or 1 and l are easily confused. Use the 'show password' option while typing. The factory password is usually on a label on the router (WPA key, Wireless key, Network key) – unless someone changed it.

l_restart.title: Restart laptop and router
l_restart.text: Restart the router (power off, 30 seconds, power on, two to five minutes to start). Then restart the laptop – a real restart, not just closing the lid.

l_random.title: Switch off random (private) hardware addresses for this network
l_random.text: With this option the laptop presents a different hardware (MAC) address to the network. Routers with a MAC filter or device approval list then treat it as an unknown device and refuse it.

paths.win11: Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > (your network) properties > Random hardware addresses
paths.win10: Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi > Random hardware addresses
paths.macnew: System Settings > Wi-Fi > Details… next to your network > Private Wi-Fi address (on recent macOS versions)

l_random.undo: Switch the option back on for this network.

l_security.title: Check the router's Wi-Fi security mode
l_security.text: In the router's app or admin page, look at the Wi-Fi security setting. 'WPA2/WPA3' mixed (transition) mode works with old and new devices; 'WPA3 only' locks out older laptops. Never switch to WEP or an open network – both are insecure. Also check for a MAC filter or device limit.
l_security.undo: Set the security mode back to the value you noted before the change.

l_reset.title: Reset the laptop's network settings
l_reset.text: Windows' Network reset removes every saved Wi-Fi network, VPN connection and custom network setting and reinstalls the adapters. The PC restarts by itself after about five minutes – save open work first. Do it only after the other steps, with passwords at hand.

paths.win11: Settings > Network & internet > Advanced network settings > Network reset
paths.win10: Settings > Network & Internet > Status > Network reset
paths.macnew: No single reset on a Mac: forget the network, restart, and install macOS updates
paths.macold: No single reset on a Mac: forget the network, restart, and install macOS updates

l_reset.undo: There is no undo; join your Wi-Fi networks again and reinstall VPN apps.

l_router_restart.title: Restart the router
l_router_restart.text: Unplug the router (and modem, if separate) for 30 seconds, plug the modem in first, then the router, and wait two to five minutes. Don't press the recessed Reset button – that is a factory reset.

l_support.title: Contact the laptop maker through its official site
l_support.text: If the Wi-Fi hardware is missing or keeps failing, it may need repair. Use the support contact on the manufacturer's official website or your receipt – not a number from an ad or a pop-up. The fix log on this page shows support what you already checked.

q_what.q: What exactly happens when you try to connect?

answers.label: My network isn't in the list
It's listed, but connecting fails or the password is rejected

q_any.q: With Wi-Fi on and Airplane mode off – does the laptop see any networks at all?

answers.label: Yes, neighbors' networks – just not mine
Wi-Fi was off – now my network shows up

q_adapter.q: Is the Wi-Fi adapter present and working?

answers.label: It was disabled – enabled it, now networks appear
Warning sign, or no Wi-Fi adapter listed
It looks fine, but still no networks

q_others_see.q: Do other devices see and use your network right now?

answers.label: Yes, phones and other devices use it

q_close.q: Does your network appear when the laptop is right next to the router?

q_password.q: Forget the network, then join with the password typed carefully. Does it connect?

answers.label: No – it still fails or keeps asking for the password

q_phone.q: Can a phone join the same network with the same password?

answers.label: No, the phone is refused too

q_restart.q: Restart the router and the laptop, then try again. Does it connect?

r_nointernet.title: Joining works – the next problem is the internet
r_nointernet.text: The laptop joins the Wi-Fi, so the connection to the router is established. 'No internet' is a different problem with its own diagnosis.
r_nointernet.why: Being connected proves that the Wi-Fi password and the laptop's adapter work.

link.label: Continue with: Wi-Fi connected but no internet

r_switched_off.title: Solved: the laptop's Wi-Fi radio was off
r_switched_off.text: Airplane mode, a function key or a disabled adapter had switched the radio off. Some laptops turn it off when the battery saver kicks in or after a sleep; if it happens often, install the current Wi-Fi driver.
r_switched_off.why: Networks appeared as soon as the radio was switched on.

r_adapter.title: Likely here: the laptop's Wi-Fi adapter
r_adapter.text: Windows doesn't see a working Wi-Fi adapter. Install the driver for your exact model from the maker's support site (download it on another device and copy it over with a USB stick, or use a network cable). If no adapter is listed at all, the hardware may be disabled in the firmware or defective – contact the maker.
r_adapter.why: No networks at all, and the adapter is missing or reports an error.

r_adapter_soft.title: Likely here: the laptop's Wi-Fi software
r_adapter_soft.text: The adapter is present but finds no networks. A driver update and, as the last step, a network reset usually bring it back. If other devices nearby see networks, that confirms the laptop is the problem.
r_adapter_soft.why: The adapter is listed without errors, yet the laptop finds no networks at all – the radio's software side is the next suspect.

r_router_off.title: Likely here: the router isn't broadcasting
r_router_off.text: No device sees your network, so the router's Wi-Fi is off, restarting or broken. Check the Wi-Fi light and button on the router (some have a Wi-Fi on/off button or a schedule) and restart it.
r_router_off.why: The network is invisible to every device, not only the laptop.

r_range.title: Likely here: signal range
r_range.text: Your laptop sees the network only near the router, so the signal is too weak where you use it. Move the router to a central, raised, open spot, use a mesh system or a repeater from a known brand, or use 2.4 GHz further away.
r_range.why: The same laptop sees the network at short range.

r_band.title: Likely here: band or hidden network
r_band.text: Other devices use the network, but the laptop never sees it even up close. Either the router sends it on a band the laptop doesn't support (often 6 GHz, sometimes 5 GHz on old laptops), or the network is hidden. Add the network by name, or switch on 2.4 GHz in the router.
r_band.why: The router works for others, and distance is not the cause.

r_profile.title: Solved: an outdated saved network
r_profile.text: The laptop had stored an old password or old security settings for this network. Joining fresh created a clean profile.
r_profile.why: The same laptop connected right after the old profile was removed.

r_router_pw.title: Likely here: the router's password or access rules
r_router_pw.text: A phone is refused with the same password, so the password is wrong or the router refuses new devices – through a MAC filter, a device limit, or 'new device approval' in a router app. Check the router's app or admin page, or the label if the password was never changed.
r_router_pw.why: Two different devices fail with the same password.

r_restart.title: Solved: the restart cleared it
r_restart.text: Either the router or the laptop had a stuck Wi-Fi state. If it returns, update the laptop's Wi-Fi driver and ask your provider about router firmware.
r_restart.why: The connection worked after restarting both ends.

r_compat.title: Likely here: a mismatch between laptop and router
r_compat.text: Phones join, the laptop doesn't – even after restarts. Common causes are random hardware addresses meeting a router filter, WPA3-only security on an older laptop, or an outdated Wi-Fi driver. Work through the steps in order; the network reset is the last one.
r_compat.why: The router accepts other devices with the same password, so the laptop's side of the handshake is the difference.
